tsk_01M50SGGCEZ4PY.title: Implement the pure, immutable game engine at src/game/engine.ts with the exact export contract
tsk_01M50SGGCEZ4PY.action:
Write src/game/engine.ts exporting exactly Status, Cell, Revealed, Game, Options, DIFFICULTIES (beginner 9/9/10, intermediate 16/16/40, expert 16/30/99), createGame, reveal, toggleFlag, chord and minesLeft. The module must import nothing and reference no DOM, timers, localStorage or Math.random; the only randomness is an internal seeded PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) keyed by (seed, rows, cols, firstRow, firstCol). Implement all eleven rules: immutable calls returning the same object reference when nothing changes; RangeError outside rows/cols 5–50 and mines 1–rows×cols−9; layout option fixing the board exactly while ignoring given rows/cols/mines but still validating size; first-reveal mine placement never on the clicked cell or its neighbours with all cells mine:false/adjacent:0 until then; status transitions ready→playing, lost on mine, won when every non-mine is revealed, and frozen once won/lost; flood fill over zero cells plus bordering numbered cells skipping flagged cells; lastRevealed distances computed by BFS passing only through zero cells (chord origin distance 0 but not newly revealed); loss revealing every mine while flags stay; win flagging every mine; toggleFlag on hidden cells only, more flags allowed than mines; chord routing through reveal so a wrong flag can lose, no-op when flagged-neighbour count ≠ number; minesLeft = mines − flags, possibly negative.

tsk_01M50SGGCE0TTR.action: Implement src/main.ts and supporting modules (src/ui/) rendering from engine state only: #board as role=grid with one role=row per row of button[role=gridcell] cells carrying data-row/data-col/data-state (hidden|flagged|revealed|mine|wrong-flag), data-exploded on the losing mine, number text for adjacent>0 and aria-labels; #status with data-status and human text; #mines-left from minesLeft; #timer in whole seconds starting at 0, stopping on end, capped at 999; #new-game restarting the same kind; #difficulty select persisting across reloads; #best-time per board key (per difficulty and per ?board value) showing an em dash when none; #mute with aria-pressed persisted. Wire left-click reveal, right-click flag with contextmenu preventDefault, left-click chord on revealed numbers; roving tabindex (exactly one cell tabindex=0, arrows move focus and stop at edges, Enter/Space reveal-or-chord, F flags, visible focus); synchronous state updates in the same task as input. Pure logic: no DOM, no timers, no Math.random except as described for seed. These exports, with these names and shapes:
export type Status = 'ready' | 'playing' | 'won' | 'lost';
export interface Revealed { row: number; col: number; distance: number }
export const DIFFICULTIES: { beginner: { rows: 9; cols: 9; mines: 10 }; intermediate: { rows: 16; cols: 16; mines: 40 }; expert: { rows: 16; cols: 30; mines: 99 }; };
Immutable. No function changes the Game it is given. A call that changes nothing returns the very same object it was given.
rows and cols are integers from 5 to 50, and mines from 1 to rows × cols − 9. Anything else makes createGame throw a RangeError.
With layout, the board is exactly that grid: rows, cols and mines come from it (any given are ignored), mines never move, and adjacent is set from the start. The size rule still applies.
Without layout, mines are placed at the first reveal: exactly mines of them, never on the revealed cell or any of its neighbours.
With a seed, the placement depends only on the seed, the board size and the first cell. Until placement every cell has adjacent: 0 and mine: false.
ready until the first reveal, then playing; lost when a mine is revealed; won when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags are not needed). Once won or lost, every function returns the game unchanged.
Revealing a hidden, unflagged cell reveals it. If it has adjacent: 0, its neighbours are revealed too, and so on outward... Flagged cells are never revealed this way.

lastRevealed lists every cell the call revealed, each with its distance: 0 for the clicked cell, otherwise the fewest steps from the clicked cell to it, moving one neighbour at a time and passing only through revealed zero cells. Revealing a revealed or flagged cell changes nothing.
Loss. Revealing a mine reveals every mine, and the game is lost. Flags stay where they are.
Win. When the game is won, every mine is flagged.
toggleFlag flags or unflags a hidden cell; on a revealed cell it changes nothing. There may be more flags than mines.
lastRevealed measures distance from the chorded cell, which is 0 but not itself newly revealed.
minesLeft is mines minus the number of flagged cells; it can be negative.
Mouse: left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu appears); left click on a revealed number chords.

the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has tabindex="0", the rest -1. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is a revealed number; F toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.
State is immediate. Cell data-state, #mines-left, #status and the rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after an animation.
Best times are kept per board: per difficulty, and per ?board value. A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.
?board= fixes the board: rows separated by ,, each a string of * (mine) and . (safe)... The game uses that layout (rule 3), and #new-game starts it again.
?seed= with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the current difficulty.
With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty (beginner the first time).
Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.

Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three notes.
